tier_reason: C stands for the same-run rows; the Serde-versus-yyjson ratio compares two runs (cross-run precedent) and is no longer the headline.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Same-run rows (2025-08-17 update, kostya/benchmarks commit 63ffa65, carried unchanged into the 2026-07-19 README): Rust (Serde Typed) 0.110 s and Rust (Serde Custom) 0.103 s versus C++/g++ RapidJSON 0.154 s (clang++ 0.194 s), about 1.4x-1.9x faster (derived from page data). Not faster than C++/g++ simdjson On-Demand 0.060 s or C++/clang++ DAW JSON Link 0.085 s; about equal to simdjson DOM 0.103 s (clang++). Rust doing like-for-like DOM parsing (Serde Untyped) takes 0.557 s, 2.9-3.6x slower than RapidJSON. The C yyjson rows (0.131/0.132 s) first appeared in the 2026-07-19 update, so the Serde Custom versus yyjson 1.27x compares two runs and toolchains (cross-run, not a valid comparison); check gason's row date before using it.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Measured toolchain for the Serde, RapidJSON and nlohmann/json rows (2025-08-17 update, commit 63ffa65; the 2026-07-19 Versions table lists newer compilers that did not produce them): Rust 1.89.0 with RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native -C llvm-args=--x86-branches-within-32B-boundaries' cargo build --release, profile lto = true, codegen-units = 1, panic = abort; serde_json 1.0.142 and serde 1.0.219. C++: g++ 14.2.0 and clang++ 19.1.7 (clang++ with -stdlib=libc++), -O3 -march=native -flto=auto -Wa,-mbranches-within-32B-boundaries -std=c++23 and no -DNDEBUG; RapidJSON built without RAPIDJSON_SSE2/SSE42. The C yyjson rows link Debian's libyyjson-dev shared library and were measured in the 2026-07-19 run.
corrections.caveats: [verifier batch-64, wave 4] The earlier toolchain (Rust 1.97.1, serde_json 1.0.150, gcc 16.1.0, clang 22.1.8) is the README's current Versions table, not what measured the Json rows; the yyjson rows come from a later run than the Serde rows. The C++ baselines keep asserts enabled (no -DNDEBUG) and RapidJSON runs without its SSE paths.
